hints.title: Subsequence State Definition
hints.text: Let state[i][j] represent the maximum length of a good subsequence ending at index i with at most j transitions.

hints.title: Transition Formulation
hints.text: For each previous index p < i, if nums[p] == nums[i], extend with 0 extra cost: dp[p][j] + 1; otherwise with 1 cost: dp[p][j - 1] + 1.

hints.title: Global Optimum
hints.text: The maximum value among all dp[i][j] across all indices and j <= k is the answer.

hints.title: Implementation

complexity.notes: Quadratic iteration over previous elements for each of the k + 1 transition levels.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Exponential 2^n brute force subsequence generation cannot pass n = 500.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n * k) table stores subsequence length per index and transition count.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Define clean 2D DP state indexed by element and allowed mismatch count.
